Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇}} (Fire, Southeast, Snake, Fear, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Suzaku|en|朱雀}} (Fire, South, Arguments, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Rikugō|ja|六合 (十二天将)}} (Wood, East, Harmony, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kōchin|ja|勾陳}} (Earth, Southeast, Conflict, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Seiryū|en|青竜}} (Wood, Northeast, Wealth, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kijin|ja|天一神}} (Earth, Northeast, Good fortune, Auspicious) # {{ill|Tenkō (goddess)|ja|媽祖}} (Water, Northwest, Women, Auspicious) # {{ill|Taiin|ja|太陰}} (Metal, West, Concealment, Auspicious) # {{ill|Genbu|en|玄武}} (Water, North, Theft, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Taijō|ja|太常}} (Earth, Southwest, Clothing, Auspicious) # {{ill|Byakko|en|白虎}} (Metal, Southwest, Disease, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Tenkū|ja|天空}} (Earth, Northwest, Deception, Inauspicious) ==Works featuring Jūni Tenshō== # {{ill|Shōnen Onmyōji|en|少年陰陽師}} (Yūki Mitsuru) # {{ill|Tokyo Majin Gakuen Gehōchō|ja|東京魔人學園外法帖}} (Shout Design Works) # {{ill|Nandakakowaremaru|ja|なんだかコワレ丸}} (Yaya Akihisa) # {{ill|Yamigami Kō|ja|闇神コウ〜暗闇にドッキリ!〜}} (Kaji Kimiya) # {{ill|Yami no Matsuei|en|闇の末裔}} (Matsushita Yoko) # {{ill|Hengen Taima Yakō Karura Mau!|ja|カルラ舞う!}} (Nagakubo Takakazu) # {{ill|Tokyo Ravens|en|東京レイヴンズ}} (Azano Kōhei) # {{ill|Ware, Tenmei o Kutsugaesu Onmyōji Abe no Seimei|ja|我、天命を覆す 陰陽師・安倍晴明}} (Yūki Mitsuru) # {{ill|Sōsei no Onmyōji|en|双星の陰陽師}} (Sukeno Yoshiaki) # {{ill|Onmyōji Genyaroku: Waga Tenohira de Nemure|ja|-陰陽師幻夜録- 我が掌で眠れ}} (Rejet) # {{ill|Dark Gathering|en|ダークギャザリング}} (Kondō Kenichi) # {{ill|Taiyō to Tsuki no Hagane|ja|太陽と月の鋼}} (Matsuura Daruma) ==See Also== # {{ill|Shikisen|ja|式占}} # Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, Southeast, Snake, Fear, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Suzaku|en|朱雀|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, South, Arguments, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Rikugō|ja|六合 (十二天将)|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, East, Harmony, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kōchin|ja|勾陳|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southeast, Conflict, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Seiryū|en|青竜|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, Northeast, Wealth, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kijin|ja|天一神|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Northeast, Good fortune, Auspicious) # {{ill|Tenkō (goddess)|ja|媽祖|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, Northwest, Women, Auspicious) # {{ill|Taiin|ja|太陰|12=draft|12=draft}} (Metal, West, Concealment, Auspicious) # {{ill|Genbu|en|玄武|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, North, Theft, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Taijō|ja|太常|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southwest, Clothing, Auspicious) # {{ill|Byakko|en|白虎|12=draft|12=draft}} (Metal, Southwest, Disease, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Tenkū|ja|天空|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Northwest, Deception, Inauspicious) ==Works featuring Jūni Tenshō== # {{ill|Shōnen Onmyōji|en|少年陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} (Yūki Mitsuru) # {{ill|Tokyo Majin Gakuen Gehōchō|ja|東京魔人學園外法帖|12=draft|12=draft}} (Shout Design Works) # {{ill|Nandakakowaremaru|ja|なんだかコワレ丸|12=draft|12=draft}} (Yaya Akihisa) # {{ill|Yamigami Kō|ja|闇神コウ〜暗闇にドッキリ!〜|12=draft|12=draft}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, Southeast, Snake, Fear, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Suzaku|en|朱雀|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, South, Arguments, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Rikugō|ja|六合 (十二天将)|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, East, Harmony, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kōchin|ja|勾陳|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southeast, Conflict, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Seiryū|en|青竜|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}}[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, Southeast, Snake, Fear, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Suzaku|en|朱雀|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, South, Arguments, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Rikugō|ja|六合 (十二天将)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, East, Harmony, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kōchin|ja|勾陳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southeast, Conflict, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Seiryū|en|青竜|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, Northeast, Wealth, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kijin|ja|天一神|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Northeast, Good fortune, Auspicious) # {{ill|Tenkō (goddess)|ja|媽祖|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, Northwest, Women, Auspicious) # {{ill|Taiin|ja|太陰|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Metal, West, Concealment, Auspicious) # {{ill|Genbu|en|玄武|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, North, Theft, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Taijō|ja|太常|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southwest, Clothing, Auspicious) # Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, Southeast, Snake, Fear, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Suzaku|en|朱雀|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, South, Arguments, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Rikugō|ja|六合 (十二天将)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, East, Harmony, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kōchin|ja|勾陳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southeast, Conflict, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Seiryū|en|青竜|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, Northeast, Wealth, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kijin|ja|天一神|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Northeast, Good fortune, Auspicious) # {{ill|Tenkō (goddess)|ja|媽祖|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, Northwest, Women, Auspicious) # {{ill|Taiin|ja|太陰|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Metal, West, Concealment, Auspicious) # {{ill|Genbu|en|玄武|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, North, Theft, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Taijō|ja|太常|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southwest, Clothing, Auspicious) # {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, Southeast, Snake, Fear, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Suzaku|en|朱雀|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Fire, South, Arguments, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Rikugō|ja|六合 (十二天将)|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, East, Harmony, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kōchin|ja|勾陳|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southeast, Conflict, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Seiryū|en|青竜|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Wood, Northeast, Wealth, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kijin|ja|天一神|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Northeast, Good fortune, Auspicious) # {{ill|Tenkō (goddess)|ja|媽祖|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, Northwest, Women, Auspicious) # {{ill|Taiin|ja|太陰|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Metal, West, Concealment, Auspicious) # {{ill|Genbu|en|玄武|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Water, North, Theft, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Taijō|ja|太常|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} (Earth, Southwest, Clothing, Auspicious) # Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|12=draft|12=draft|12=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|qq=draft}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|qq=draft}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|qq=draft}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|qq=draft}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|qq=draft}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|qq=draft}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|qq=draft}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|qq=draft}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|qq=draft}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|qq=draft}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). }} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|qq=}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill|qq=}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|qq=draft|qq=}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018|qq=}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|qq=draft|qq=}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|qq=draft|qq=}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|qq=draft|qq=}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|qq=draft|qq=}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|qq=draft|qq=}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|qq=draft|qq=}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|qq=draft|qq=}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|qq=draft|qq=}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|qq=draft|qq=}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|qq=draft|qq=}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). |qq=}} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly Generals)|ja|騰蛇|qq=draft|qq=}} (Fire, Southeast, Snake, Fear, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Suzaku|en|朱雀|qq=draft|qq=}} (Fire, South, Arguments, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Rikugō|ja|六合 (十二天将)|qq=draft|qq=}} (Wood, East, Harmony, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kōchin|ja|勾陳|qq=draft|qq=}} (Earth, Southeast, Conflict, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Seiryū|en|青竜|qq=draft|qq=}} (Wood, Northeast, Wealth, Auspicious) # {{ill|Kijin|ja|天一神|qq=draft|qq=}} (Earth, Northeast, Good fortune, Auspicious) # {{ill|Tenkō (goddess)|ja|媽祖|qq=draft|qq=}} (Water, Northwest, Women, Auspicious) # {{ill|Taiin|ja|太陰|qq=draft|qq=}} (Metal, West, Concealment, Auspicious) # {{ill|Genbu|en|玄武|qq=draft|qq=}} (Water, North, Theft, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Taijō|ja|太常|qq=draft|qq=}} (Earth, Southwest, Clothing, Auspicious) # {{ill|Byakko|en|白虎|qq=draft|qq=}} (Metal, Southwest, Disease, Inauspicious) # {{ill|Tenkū|ja|天空|qq=draft|qq=}} (Earth, Northwest, Deception, Inauspicious) ==Works featuring Jūni Tenshō== # {{出典の明記|date=2018年8月}} '''十二天将'''（じゅうにてんしょう）は、[[安倍晴明]]をはじめとする[[陰陽師]]にとって必須の占術であった[[六壬神課]]で使用する象徴体系の一つである。[[北極星]]を中心とする星や[[星座]]に起源を持っており、それぞれが[[陰陽五行思想|陰陽五行説]]に当てはまる。 十二天将は[[十二神将]]と呼ばれる事も多々あるが、'''仏教'''の[[十二天]]、[[十二神将]]とは全くの別物。六壬鑰等の六壬の古典では『神』は六壬天地盤の天盤に配される十二支であり『将』は十二天将を指している。そのため六壬神課における『神将』は、天盤十二支とそれに配布された十二天将の両方を同時によぶ用語であって、十二天将を十二神将と呼ぶのは本来は正しくない。 ==一覧== [[陰陽師]]として名高い[[安倍晴明]]が残した[[占事略决]]の第4章の「十二将所主法第四」では十二天将が表す事柄について以下のように解説されている。 {{Quotation| 前一騰虵火神家在巳主驚恐怖畏凶将 前二朱雀火神家在午主口舌懸官凶将 前三六合木神家在卯主陰私和合吉将 前四勾陳土神家在辰主戦闘諍訟凶将 前五青竜木神家在寅主銭財慶賀吉将 天一貴人上神家在丑主福徳之神吉将大无成 後一天后水神家在亥主後宮婦女吉将 後二大陰金神家在酉主弊匿隠蔵吉将 後三玄武水神家在子主亡遺盗賊凶将 後四大裳土神家在未主冠帯衣服吉将 後五白虎金神家在申主疾病喪凶将 後六天空土神家在戌主欺殆不信凶将 }} 『名称参考：日本陰陽道史総説より』 表にし、異名などを補うと次のとおり。 {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:95%; {{afc comment|1=Apparently different from {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|qq=}} Here's your translation with proper use of the "{{ill|qq=}}" template: [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 18:09, 3 March 2025 (UTC)|qq=draft|qq=}} {{Unreferenced|date=August 2018|qq=}} '''Jūni Tenshō''' (十二天将, lit. Twelve Heavenly Generals) refers to a symbolic system used within the {{ill|Rokujin Shinka|ja|六壬神課|qq=draft|qq=}} divination method, which was essential for {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|qq=draft|qq=}} practitioners such as {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|qq=draft|qq=}}. Originating from constellations centered around the {{ill|Polaris|en|北極星|qq=draft|qq=}}, each corresponds to principles of {{ill|Yin-Yang and the Five Elements|en|陰陽五行思想|qq=draft|qq=}}. Although frequently called {{ill|Jūni Shinshō|ja|十二神将|qq=draft|qq=}}, Jūni Tenshō differs significantly from the Buddhist {{ill|Twelve Devas|ja|十二天|qq=draft|qq=}} and {{ill|Twelve Heavenly Generals|en|十二神将|qq=draft|qq=}}. In traditional texts like "Rokujin Yaku," the term "Kami" (神) refers specifically to the twelve Earthly Branches (十二支) placed on the heavenly board (天盤), and "Shō" (将) denotes the Twelve Heavenly Generals themselves. Therefore, "Kami-Shō" (神将) refers simultaneously to both the Twelve Branches and their corresponding Twelve Generals, and strictly speaking, labeling Jūni Tenshō as Jūni Shinshō is incorrect. ==List== {{ill|Abe no Seimei|en|安倍晴明|qq=draft|qq=}}, a renowned {{ill|Onmyōji|ja|陰陽師|qq=draft|qq=}}, in Chapter 4 of his work "Senji Ryakuketsu" (占事略决), explains the characteristics associated with each of the Twelve Generals as follows: {{Quotation| '''Former Deities (前):''' * '''First:''' The Soaring Snake, Fire Deity resides in *Si (巳)* – governs fear, terror, and ominous generals (凶将). * '''Second:''' The Vermilion Bird, Fire Deity resides in *Wu (午)* – governs disputes, arguments, and official entanglements (凶将). * '''Third:''' The Six Harmonies, Wood Deity resides in *Mao (卯)* – governs secrecy and harmony, auspicious generals (吉将). * '''Fourth:''' The Hooked Chen, Earth Deity resides in *Chen (辰)* – governs battles, lawsuits, and strife (凶将). * '''Fifth:''' The Azure Dragon, Wood Deity resides in *Yin (寅)* – governs wealth, fortune, and celebration (吉将). * '''Heavenly Nobleman:''' Supreme Deity resides in *Chou (丑)* – governs blessings and virtue, deity of good fortune (吉将), but ends with "Great Nothingness Achieved" (大无成 – possibly an idiom or esoteric phrase meaning culmination or void success). --- '''Later Deities (後):''' * '''First:''' The Queen of Heaven, Water Deity resides in *Hai (亥)* – governs the inner palace and women, auspicious general (吉将). * '''Second:''' The Great Yin, Metal Deity resides in *You (酉)* – governs secrets, concealment, and hidden matters (吉将). * '''Third:''' The Black Tortoise, Water Deity resides in *Zi (子)* – governs loss, theft, and banditry (凶将). * '''Fourth:''' The Great Skirt, Earth Deity resides in *Wei (未)* – governs clothing, robes, and ceremonial dress (吉将). * '''Fifth:''' The White Tiger, Metal Deity resides in *Shen (申)* – governs illness and death (凶将). * '''Sixth:''' The Sky Void, Earth Deity resides in *Xu (戌)* – governs deception, danger, and mistrust (凶将). |qq=}} ("Names Reference: Nihon Onmyōdōshi Sōsetsu") The above information is organized below, with aliases included: # {{ill|Tōda (Twelve Heavenly
